"Ordinarily when a first information report is lodged soon after the occurrence leaving no scope for consultation and fabrication the presumption is that it is a truthful account eliminating the possibility of substitution or false implication." 

 41. Lastly, Mr Malek argues that although Biplob, son of the victim, was allegedly an eye-witness, but he was not examined in Court, in spite of his name being mentioned in the charge-sheet and, as such, there is a strong presumption that the occurrence might not have happened in the manner as stated by the other witnesses and since he was not examined, the whole prosecution story is false. 

 42. It appears from the deposition of PW 1 that at the time of trial, Biplob was away from the country, as such, the question of his examination does not arise. Since, other eye-witnesses, specially PW 1, mother of Biplob and PW 2 were examined. Besides PW 6, brother of Biplob, was also examined, as such, there is no scope for any presumption that the occurrence did not happen as proved by the prosecution witnesses.
